Issued at 102 AM CDT Thu Oct 29 2026

As of 1am, not a cloud in the sky over the region which is leading 
to a good amount of radiational cooling with current temps in the 
lower 30s to the lower 40s (coldest over north central SD) and winds 
calm to light out of the west and northwest. This flow is also 
helping to keep fog from forming, however, starting to see some 
patchy fog forming over portions of southeastern SD. ConsShort still 
tries to indicate slight viz reductions occurring over portions
of northeastern SD through the morning but as mentioned this 
should be very patchy at most and not as thick as yesterday 
morning.

Mostly dry conditions and near normal temperatures are expected 
today through the day Friday as the region is within a broad ridging 
pattern and a 1023mb surface high pressure over the area. However, 
within this zonal to slight southwest flow, weak spotty shortwave 
activity tracks northeast/east within the ridge as CAMs indicate 
there could be just enough 700mb lift/moisture to produce spotty 
showers that would track across the CWA early this morning 
through the afternoon. NBM shows the potential for this but 
keeps pops about 10-20%. ECAM of course shows a bit higher pops 
ranging from 20-40% while REFS also keeps chances low. This is 
likely due to the dry air at ~800mb to the surface which will 
make it hard for any rain to reach the surface. So if it does, 
then mostly likely sprinkles or it will stay as virga. Not 
enough confidence to use the ECAM (or even a blend at this 
point) and stuck with the NBM. This may need to be adjusted if 
in fact we do see precip. Otherwise, this ridge amplifies Friday
(and tilts negatively from west central Canada and 
southwestward) as this high pressure exits the region to the 
east/northeast. Additional high pressure (and stronger) develops
(and merges with the previous one) that extends from south 
central Canada and southeastward through WI/MN. This will track 
southeastward through Friday, which will clip the northern and 
northeastern CWA.

Our next chance of precipitation will be Friday afternoon into 
Saturday as a large closed mid level low is forecast to hover just 
off the Pacific Northwest coast and really just spinning in place 
through Saturday. This results in a negatively tilted shortwave 
developing on the PVA side of it as it will track north and 
northeastward from NM/TX into the central plains. In combination 
with a surface warm front also lifting northward, rain showers will 
track north/northeast and entering south central SD ~late Friday 
afternoon with the light rain expanding across the CWA before 
exiting the northeastern CWA late Saturday morning/midday. This 
looks to be a weak system therefore NBM pops range from 20-50%, 
highest over south central through east central SD with pops 
diminishing further north you in the CWA. Probability of QPF of 
0.10" or more is 20 to 40% east of the Missouri River with the 
highest pops over east central SD.

As this large wave moves onshore Sunday and tracks east over the 
Intermountain west, a Colorado low (with an inverted trough 
extending northward through the Northern Rockies) develops late 
Sunday/early Monday and will track eastward/northeast (becoming 
quite elongated) through early next week. As of now ENS is further 
northwest with the position of the low than GEFS by 06Z Monday with 
GEFS being more southerly with the track than ENS along with GEFS 
indicating a few millibars stronger with the low. So high confidence 
on this setup but low confidence on exact track/strength which leads 
to low confidence on QPF amounts and where the highest amounts will 
be at this time. Latest NBM has widespread 60-90% pops moving in 
early Monday with the rain tracking eastward with pops diminishing 
west to east across the CWA ~Tuesday night or early Wednesday (model 
depending). As of now the bulk of the rain (and highest pops) looks 
to fall Monday morning through Tuesday morning. Probability of a 
half inch of rain 12Z Monday-12Z Tuesday is 30-50% (lowest north 
central SD) per grand ensemble mean (ENS/GEFS/GEPS) with ENS being 
the most aggressive on this QPF chance while GEFS is less aggressive 
(give more of a southerly track for now). NBM is 40-75%. Again low 
confidence in exact totals but all models indicate the bulk of the 
precip will be from south central through NESD/MN. This system will 
have moisture to work with as higher PWAT values of 0.75 to 1" will 
expand northward on the warm side of the low with values running 3 
to 4 standard deviation above climo per NAEFS. It is also 
interesting to note that EC EFI is already highlighting values 
of 0.6 to 0.8 for QPF with a shift of tails of 1 for Monday. So 
still kind of on the low side meaning most members are near the 
reforecast climatology and the "boom" potential is low for now. 
However, this is several days out. As mentioned, Ptype is
